Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via PeeringDB (9 peers/connections, 18G total capacity) and the Internet Society's ISOC Pulse IXP Tracker, which lists around 8 members including Togocom (10 Gbps port), CAFE Informatique, and PCH route servers. This supports 'Active IXP(s) with moderate participation'; Value Code 4 confirmed.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataReportal/GSMA Intelligence figures for Togo are for cellular mobile connections (SIM-based: 75.5% in Jan 2024, 86.0% in Oct 2025), not unique-subscriber penetration as the variable specifically requires — the cited 78.2% figure does not match either published report and appears to conflate the two distinct metrics. GSMA's Mobile Economy Sub-Saharan Africa 2024 report puts regional unique-subscriber penetration at only ~44% in 2023, and Togo scores just 42.2 on GSMA's Mobile Connectivity Index ('Emerging' cluster), suggesting Togo's true unique-subscriber rate is materially below the 70%+ band scored. No Togo-specific GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber percentage could be located in open sources; flagged for human review rather than guessed.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: Law No. 2019-014 (29 October 2019) on personal data protection, implemented via Decree 2020-111/PR, established the IPDCP (Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel), which is active with its own website and a mandate to handle complaints, authorise foreign data transfers, and sanction breaches. A 2024 World Bank project document notes the IPDCP was 'currently being operationalised', consistent with an established but still-maturing authority. Value Code 4 confirmed.

Definition: Affordability of electricity for residential and small business consumers, measured as cost of electricity relative to income levels. High electricity costs are a direct barrier to ICT adoption and data center viability.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed current CEET residential tariffs (effective 15 May 2025): a subsidised 'social' tranche of 60-70 FCFA/kWh for the first 30 kWh, rising to 93-130 FCFA/kWh (~USD 0.10-0.22) thereafter. Depending on assumed monthly consumption (30-50 kWh, typical for lower-income households), this equates to roughly 3.6-7.2% of monthly GNI per capita (~US$84), straddling the 'Moderate (3-5%)' and 'Expensive (6-10%)' bands. The original comment's own arithmetic (implying ~1.8%/month) is inconsistent with the Code 2 result it was attached to. Value code left unchanged pending a standardised consumption assumption; flagged for human review.
